text: Engine prefill on CUDA vs llama.cpp
hanzo-engine against llama.cpp on CUDA, built against the same weights and run on the same box: prefill throughput at the prompt lengths where the whole 95% interval of the ratio lies above parity.
prints the table on this page — transcribed from the committed run files on branch bench/dossier, the pass of 2026-07-21

hanzo-engine and llama.cpp, built against the same weights, run on the same box, alternating. Prefill is tokens per second at a given prompt length, and the ratio is ours over theirs, so above 1.000 is a win. The models are Zen-1.7B at Q4_K_M and Zen-4B at Q4_K_M; 7 repetitions per cell, as its run records, with the first discarded as warmup, a Student-t 95% interval on each engine, and the ratio's interval formed by adding the two relative intervals in quadrature.
The verdict is the harness's, not a reading of ours:
where the whole interval lies above 1.000 and neither engine's coefficient of variation exceeded 5%, which is how the harness says the box was quiet. Every cell below is one.
